name: Hiroshi Yoshimura

sonic_profile.texture: minimal, clean — keyboard and Fender Rhodes, sparse layering
sonic_profile.density: very low — each sound placed with intention, silence is structural
sonic_profile.energy: contemplative, undemanding — music that coexists with the room rather than filling it

philosophical_profile: Yoshimura's kankyo ongaku is not background music — it's music that sharpens awareness of environment. Where Eno creates a landscape to inhabit, Yoshimura turns attention toward the landscape already present. He described composing by 'catching the waves of the scenery out of the window,' treating natural phenomena — rain, shade, cloud movement — as compositional partners, not just inspiration. Sound as a way of noticing, not constructing. The architecture of the listening space is as much part of the work as the notes.

sources.summary: Scene retrospective — kankyo ongaku philosophy, compositional approach, relationship to Eno's ambient concept.
Spencer Doran on kankyo ongaku tradition — Yoshimura as central figure, the philosophy of sound in space.
